fixture: Drug Interaction Screen - blind test fixture
how_to_use: Feed the app only the `lists` array. Each list is a patient medication list as a US prescriber would enter it, with no hint of what is wrong. Compare the app's output to `answer_key`, which is a separate top-level object so it can be stripped before the run.

scoring.hit: The app flags the same drugs (or a superset) under an equivalent category at the same or higher severity.
scoring.miss: An `expected` item the app does not flag.
scoring.false_positive: Anything in `should_not_flag` reported at moderate or higher, or any moderate-or-higher flag on a control list.
scoring.totals: Where `totals` is present, the app should compute that per-molecule daily amount after merging duplicate lines, brands, and combination-product components.

schema.medication.brand: Brand name as typed by the prescriber. null means only the generic was entered.
schema.medication.generic: Generic name. Combination products list every component separated by '/'.
schema.medication.strength: Unit dose as written on the prescription. Units are as written: mg, mcg, mEq, g, units, mcg/h.
schema.medication.frequency: As written. PRN entries state the maximum doses per day.
schema.medication.total_daily: Amount per day as written for that line only. 'max' for PRN; per-week for weekly drugs; per-episode where a daily number does not exist.
schema.medication.otc: Present and true only for over-the-counter products.
schema.answer_key.<id>.theme: What the list was built to test.
schema.answer_key.<id>.totals: Per-molecule daily totals the app should arrive at.
schema.answer_key.<id>.should_not_flag: Drugs or pairs with no clinically significant interaction in that list.

L01.theme: Same drug entered twice; sedative stacking; stimulant above labeled maximum

expected.why: Two Zyprexa lines are one drug. Daily olanzapine is 12.5 mg, not 10 or 2.5.
Benzodiazepine + Z-drug + sedating antipsychotic: additive sedation, respiratory depression, falls. Zolpidem + a benzodiazepine is also duplicate sedative-hypnotic therapy.
60 mg/day exceeds the Adderall IR labeled maximum of 40 mg/day.
Stimulant against a benzodiazepine and a D2 antagonist; effects partly cancel.

L02.theme: Serotonin syndrome cluster; PRN max dosing

expected.why: Five serotonergic agents: SSRI, tramadol (reuptake inhibitor + opioid), triptan, cyclobenzaprine (tricyclic-like), ondansetron (FDA 2012 label warning). Sertraline + tramadol alone is major.
Tramadol lowers seizure threshold; SSRI co-use raises the risk.
5-HT3 blockade may reduce tramadol analgesia.

L03.theme: QT prolongation; CYP2C19 inhibition pushing citalopram past its cap; diuretic electrolyte loss

expected.why: Four QT-prolonging drugs; torsades risk is additive. Citalopram's QT effect is dose-dependent.
Fluconazole inhibits CYP2C19. Celexa label caps citalopram at 20 mg/day with CYP2C19 inhibitors; 40 mg here is over the cap.
CYP3A4 inhibition raises haloperidol; more QT and EPS risk.
Loop-diuretic hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia amplify QT risk.

should_not_flag: pantoprazole at moderate or above (weak CYP2C19 effect; not the omeprazole-class problem)

L04.theme: Lithium toxicity from three renal-handling interactions; triple whammy; metformin + topiramate

expected.why: ACE inhibitor reduces lithium clearance; levels can rise several-fold over weeks.
Thiazide sodium loss increases proximal lithium reabsorption; roughly 25-40% level rise.
NSAID lowers renal prostaglandins and lithium clearance; 2,400 mg/day is a full anti-inflammatory dose.
Triple whammy: ACE inhibitor + diuretic + NSAID -> acute kidney injury.
Topiramate (carbonic anhydrase inhibition) and metformin both predispose to metabolic acidosis; Topamax label warns.
HCTZ raises topiramate exposure ~30%; both cause hypokalemia.

L05.theme: Warfarin potentiation; multi-agent bleeding; alternating-day dosing; combination product

expected.why: Sulfamethoxazole inhibits CYP2C9 (S-warfarin) and displaces warfarin from albumin; INR often rises sharply within days.
Amiodarone inhibits CYP2C9 and 3A4; warfarin usually needs a 30-50% cut, and the effect persists for weeks after amiodarone stops.
Triple antithrombotic therapy: anticoagulant plus two antiplatelets.
SSRI platelet serotonin depletion adds GI bleeding risk on top of antithrombotics.
Both prolong QT; escitalopram's effect is dose-dependent.

totals.warfarin: 5 mg Mon/Wed/Fri, 2.5 mg other days = 25 mg/week; there is no single daily number

L06.theme: Opioid + benzodiazepine boxed warning; ER and IR of one opioid; MME; sedative burden

expected.why: Two brands, one molecule: 60 mg scheduled + up to 60 mg PRN = 120 mg/day oxycodone = 180 MME (CDC: reassess at 50, avoid 90+).
FDA boxed warning: opioid + benzodiazepine -> profound sedation, respiratory depression, death.
FDA 2019 warning: gabapentinoid + opioid respiratory depression.
Carisoprodol (metabolized to meprobamate) + opioid + benzodiazepine is the 'holy trinity' overdose combination.
Sedating antihistamine adds to sedation.

totals.oxycodone: 120 mg/day max (60 mg ER + 60 mg IR) = 180 MME

L07.theme: MAOI contraindications; microgram unit; PRN max

expected.why: Wellbutrin label: contraindicated with MAOIs or within 14 days; hypertensive reactions.
Meperidine + MAOI causes fatal serotonin syndrome and hyperpyrexia; label contraindication.
Ritalin label: contraindicated during or within 14 days of MAOI treatment.
MAOIs cause orthostatic hypotension; additive with antihypertensives.

L08.theme: Clozapine with opposing CYP effects; bone marrow suppression; respiratory arrest

expected.why: Both cause agranulocytosis; carbamazepine also induces CYP3A4 and cuts clozapine levels roughly in half. Avoid the combination.
Fluvoxamine is a potent CYP1A2 inhibitor; clozapine levels rise 3-5x.
Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2; clozapine levels roughly double.
Clozapine + benzodiazepine: reported respiratory and cardiac arrest, especially early in treatment.
Valproate raises carbamazepine-10,11-epoxide (toxicity); carbamazepine lowers valproate levels.
Additive QT effect.

L08.note: Net effect on clozapine is unpredictable: one inducer against two inhibitors. The app should surface both directions, not cancel them out.

L09.theme: Duplicate SSRI; CYP2D6 inhibition of a prodrug and of a substrate; SSRI + NSAID bleeding

expected.why: Two SSRIs: no added benefit, additive serotonin syndrome risk; fluoxetine's long half-life complicates any switch.
Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors block conversion of tamoxifen to endoxifen; associated with higher breast cancer recurrence. Avoid.
Metoprolol is a CYP2D6 substrate; levels rise 2-5x -> bradycardia, hypotension.
SSRI + NSAID: 3-6x upper GI bleeding vs either alone.

L10.theme: Contraindicated statin-macrolide pair; hyperkalemia triad; mEq unit; weekly dosing

expected.why: Clarithromycin (strong CYP3A4 inhibitor) raises simvastatin roughly 10x; Zocor label contraindication.
Aldosterone antagonist + ACE inhibitor + potassium supplement.
Once weekly. Treating 15 mg as daily (105 mg/week) is a well-documented fatal error; the app must not compute a daily total for it.

should_not_flag: any pair at moderate or above; escitalopram + lisinopril hyponatremia is at most minor

L12.theme: Hidden duplicates inside combination products; acetaminophen ceiling; IR + ER summing

expected.why: Symbyax already contains 25 mg fluoxetine; adding Prozac 20 mg makes 45 mg/day of one drug written twice.
Acetaminophen 1,300 mg (Norco) + 3,000 mg (Tylenol) = 4,300 mg/day, above the 4,000 mg/day ceiling; hepatotoxicity.
IR + XR of one benzodiazepine: 2.5 mg/day total.
Opioid + benzodiazepine boxed warning; olanzapine adds sedation.
Fluoxetine blocks CYP2D6 conversion of hydrocodone to hydromorphone (less analgesia); hydrocodone is also mildly serotonergic.

L13.theme: Linezolid acting as an MAOI; serotonergic load; fentanyl patch units

expected.why: Linezolid is a reversible non-selective MAOI. Zyvox label: do not combine with SNRIs/SSRIs unless benefit outweighs risk with close monitoring.
Each adds serotonergic activity; buspirone is named in the linezolid label.
Opioid + skeletal muscle relaxant: additive CNS and respiratory depression.
Metoclopramide is serotonergic (5-HT4 agonist, 5-HT3 antagonist) on top of an SNRI.

L14.theme: Respiratory depression stacking; duplicate benzodiazepines; fentanyl MME

expected.why: Opioid + benzodiazepine boxed warning, with two benzodiazepines present.
Two benzodiazepines.
FDA 2019: gabapentinoid + opioid.
Phenothiazine antihistamine potentiates opioid respiratory depression; Phenergan label warns with opioids.
Alpha-2 agonist: additive sedation and hypotension.

L15.theme: Bradycardia and AV block; digoxin level elevation; electrolyte-driven digoxin toxicity

expected.why: Beta-blocker + non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker: additive negative chronotropy, inotropy, and AV conduction slowing.
Amiodarone inhibits P-gp; digoxin levels rise about 70%. Cut digoxin 30-50%.
Diltiazem raises digoxin 20-50%.
Four AV-nodal depressants.
Cholinesterase inhibitor vagotonic effect: bradycardia, syncope, heart block with other rate-slowing drugs.
Hypokalemia and hypomagnesemia increase digoxin toxicity and amiodarone QT risk.
Amiodarone inhibits CYP2D6 -> higher metoprolol, plus additive bradycardia.

L16.theme: Nitrate + PDE5 contraindication; additive hypotension; clonidine with a beta-blocker

expected.why: PDE5 inhibitor + nitrate: cGMP accumulation -> severe, refractory hypotension.
Same mechanism; a long-acting nitrate leaves no safe window.
Alpha-1 blocker + PDE5 inhibitor: symptomatic orthostatic hypotension; Viagra label advises a stable alpha-blocker dose first.
Additive bradycardia; if clonidine is stopped, unopposed alpha stimulation under beta-blockade causes rebound hypertensive crisis. Taper the beta-blocker first.
Additive vasodilation and orthostasis.

L17.theme: Hyperkalemia from four directions; triple whammy AKI; SGLT2 volume depletion

expected.why: Trimethoprim blocks ENaC like amiloride; with an aldosterone antagonist, an ARB, and 40 mEq KCl, hyperkalemia risk is high.
Triple whammy: RAS blocker + diuretic + NSAID -> AKI; the NSAID also blunts the ARB's BP effect.
SGLT2 osmotic diuresis plus diuretic and NSAID: volume depletion and AKI.

L18.theme: Anticholinergic burden; cholinesterase inhibitor opposed by anticholinergics; CYP2D6 raising a TCA

expected.why: Five anticholinergic drugs: delirium, urinary retention, constipation/ileus, blurred vision, falls, hyperthermia.
Anticholinergics directly oppose a cholinesterase inhibitor and worsen cognition.
Paroxetine is a strong CYP2D6 inhibitor; amitriptyline and nortriptyline levels rise -> TCA toxicity, QT prolongation, seizures; also serotonin syndrome risk.
Additive QT effect.

L19.theme: Seizure threshold at labeled maximums; CYP1A2 inhibition of theophylline; QT

expected.why: Bupropion at 450 mg (labeled max; seizure risk is dose-dependent), tramadol at 400 mg (max), theophylline, a fluoroquinolone, and an antipsychotic each lower seizure threshold.
Ciprofloxacin inhibits CYP1A2; theophylline levels can rise 20-100%+ -> seizures, arrhythmias. Cipro label: avoid or monitor levels.
Additive QT effect.
Bupropion (strong CYP2D6 inhibitor) blocks tramadol activation to O-desmethyltramadol: less analgesia, more parent-drug seizure and serotonin risk.

L20.theme: Strong CYP3A4/P-gp inducer undermining five drugs

expected.why: Rivaroxaban exposure falls about 50%; Xarelto label: avoid with combined P-gp and strong CYP3A4 inducers. Thrombosis risk.
Contraceptive failure; non-hormonal backup during and for 28 days after rifampin.
Tacrolimus levels fall sharply -> graft rejection; needs dose increase and level monitoring.
Latuda label: contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inducers.
Methadone levels drop -> opioid withdrawal within days; dose increase required.

L21.theme: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitor against benzodiazepines, a DOAC, and a statin

expected.why: Triazolam AUC rises more than 20x; profound, prolonged sedation. Both labels contraindicate.
Alprazolam AUC about 4x; Xanax label contraindicates ketoconazole and itraconazole.
Combined strong CYP3A4 + P-gp inhibitor: Eliquis label -> reduce to 2.5 mg twice daily.
Atorvastatin exposure at least doubles; 80 mg is the maximum dose -> myopathy risk.
Amlodipine exposure rises modestly; hypotension, edema.

L22.theme: Transplant regimen: azole raising tacrolimus; QT; PPI reducing mycophenolate

expected.why: Fluconazole 400 mg inhibits CYP3A4; tacrolimus rises -> nephrotoxicity, neurotoxicity, hyperkalemia. Preemptive dose reduction and levels.
Three QT-prolonging drugs.
Higher gastric pH reduces mycophenolate mofetil dissolution; MPA exposure falls 25-35%. Less of an issue with enteric-coated mycophenolate sodium.
Moderate CYP3A4 inhibition; simvastatin 40 mg is at the upper end.
Omeprazole (CYP2C19/3A4) can modestly raise tacrolimus.

L23.theme: Hypoglycemia; CYP2C9 on a sulfonylurea; beta-blocker masking; weekly injectable and unit-based dosing

expected.why: Three glucose-lowering agents; adding a GLP-1 agonist to insulin + sulfonylurea calls for dose cuts in the latter two.
Sulfamethoxazole inhibits CYP2C9 -> glipizide accumulates; severe hypoglycemia reported.
Fluoroquinolone boxed warning: dysglycemia, worst with sulfonylureas and insulin.
Non-selective beta-blockade masks tachycardia and tremor and delays glucose recovery.
Delayed gastric emptying alters oral drug absorption.

L24.theme: Duplicate therapy across three classes; hidden acetaminophen total; MME

expected.why: Two full-agonist opioids; hydrocodone 40 mg + oxycodone 20 mg is about 70 MME.
1,300 + 1,300 = 2,600 mg/day. Under the 4,000 mg ceiling: the app should compute it and not flag a ceiling breach.
Two Z-drugs at bedtime; both labels warn against other sedative-hypnotics; complex sleep behavior boxed warning.
Two NSAIDs: additive GI bleeding, renal, and cardiovascular risk with no added benefit.
Opioids + sedative-hypnotics: respiratory depression.

L25.theme: Methadone QT stacking; azole raising methadone; serotonin

expected.why: Five QT-prolonging drugs; methadone at 80 mg/day carries independent torsades risk.
Fluconazole inhibits CYP3A4, 2C9, 2C19; methadone exposure rises about 35% -> respiratory depression and more QT.
Methadone is serotonergic; SNRI co-use.
Opioid + sedating antipsychotic.
CYP3A4 inhibition raises quetiapine.

L26.theme: Valproate-lamotrigine; enzyme induction; hyperammonemia; salicylate displacement

expected.why: Valproate inhibits lamotrigine glucuronidation and about doubles its half-life -> SJS/TEN risk. Lamictal label: with valproate, bipolar maintenance dose is 100 mg/day; 200 mg here needs review.
Carbamazepine lowers lamotrigine about 40%; with valproate also present, net level is unpredictable.
Valproate raises carbamazepine-10,11-epoxide; carbamazepine lowers valproate.
Hyperammonemic encephalopathy and hypothermia; both labels warn.
Salicylate displaces valproate from albumin and inhibits its metabolism -> higher free levels; valproate thrombocytopenia plus aspirin platelet inhibition.
Carbamazepine lowers clonazepam 20-30%.
Five CNS-active agents: sedation, cognitive slowing, ataxia.

L27.theme: Dopamine antagonists opposing levodopa; MAO-B inhibitor with meperidine; serotonergic caution

expected.why: Metoclopramide blocks D2 receptors: worsens parkinsonism and negates levodopa. Avoid in Parkinson's disease.
Potent D2 antagonist; same problem. If an antipsychotic is needed, quetiapine or clozapine.
Azilect label: contraindicated with meperidine (also tramadol, methadone, dextromethorphan).
Cases reported with MAO-B inhibitors + SSRIs; use the lowest SSRI dose and monitor.
Two D2 antagonists: additive extrapyramidal symptoms, tardive dyskinesia, NMS risk.
Additive QT effect.

L28.theme: Cobicistat boosting: statin, benzodiazepine, inhaled steroid, PDE5 inhibitor, tenofovir

expected.why: Cobicistat (strong CYP3A4 inhibitor) raises atorvastatin several-fold; Prezcobix label: start at the lowest dose and titrate. 80 mg is unsafe.
Alprazolam exposure rises; prolonged sedation and respiratory depression. Monitor or switch to lorazepam.
Cobicistat blocks CYP3A4 clearance of fluticasone -> systemic corticosteroid exposure, Cushing's syndrome, adrenal suppression. Label: avoid; use beclomethasone.
Sildenafil exposure rises up to 10x; label: 25 mg no more than once per 48 hours.
Cobicistat raises tenofovir exposure and blocks tubular creatinine secretion (MATE1); serum creatinine rises without true GFR loss. Monitor renal function.

should_not_flag: any pair at moderate or above

L30.theme: Absorption and timing interactions versus one true CYP problem

expected.why: Calcium binds levothyroxine in the gut; separate by 4 hours.
Iron binds levothyroxine; separate by 4 hours.
Divalent cations chelate fluoroquinolones; cipro AUC falls up to about 40%. Take cipro 2 hours before or 6 hours after.
Iron chelation cuts cipro absorption about 50%; same spacing rule.
Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19 activation of clopidogrel; FDA: avoid omeprazole and esomeprazole, use pantoprazole.
Acid suppression reduces non-heme iron absorption.
Acid suppression modestly reduces levothyroxine absorption.

L30.note: Correct output distinguishes spacing advice from a contraindication; nothing in this list is contraindicated.

L31.theme: Additive nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity; IV routes; gram unit

expected.why: Glycopeptide + aminoglycoside: synergistic nephrotoxicity.
Observational data show higher AKI rates than vancomycin + cefepime or meropenem; part may be a creatinine-secretion artifact. Contested.
Loop diuretic + aminoglycoside: additive, sometimes permanent hearing loss.
Triple whammy with a parenteral NSAID; Toradol label warns in volume depletion and renal impairment; 5-day limit.
NSAID removes renal prostaglandin protection during nephrotoxin exposure.
NSAID + ACE inhibitor.

L32.theme: Antifolate stacking; xanthine oxidase inhibition on azathioprine; NSAID on methotrexate; weekly dosing

expected.why: Additive dihydrofolate reductase inhibition plus reduced renal MTX clearance; fatal pancytopenia reported even at low weekly doses.
Allopurinol blocks xanthine oxidase, a main 6-mercaptopurine elimination route. Reduce azathioprine to 25-33% of dose or avoid.
NSAIDs reduce MTX renal clearance; risk is mainly at high MTX doses, but 1,800 mg/day ibuprofen with 20 mg/week warrants caution.
Additive marrow suppression.
Once weekly; 20 mg/day would be lethal. The app must not compute a daily total.

L33.theme: Phenytoin: induction of contraceptive and statin; CYP2C9 inhibitors raising phenytoin; warfarin

expected.why: Contraceptive failure; non-hormonal backup needed.
Fluoxetine inhibits CYP2C9; phenytoin's saturable kinetics mean a small clearance change causes a large level rise -> ataxia, nystagmus.
Fluconazole inhibits CYP2C9 -> phenytoin toxicity; Diflucan label.
Bidirectional: early protein displacement raises INR, later induction lowers it, and phenytoin levels may rise. Monitor INR and phenytoin levels.
Fluconazole inhibits CYP2C9 -> INR rises sharply.
SSRI antiplatelet effect plus mild CYP2C9 inhibition.
CYP3A4 induction lowers atorvastatin exposure.

L34.theme: Duplicate alpha-2 agonists; CYP2D6 inhibition of atomoxetine; stimulant + SSRI; sedation and hypotension

expected.why: Two central alpha-2 agonists: hypotension, bradycardia, sedation; abrupt stop -> rebound hypertension.
Strong CYP2D6 inhibitor raises atomoxetine exposure 6-8x (poor-metabolizer phenotype). Strattera label: start 40 mg, go to 80 mg only after 4 weeks if needed.
Two ADHD agents raising heart rate and BP; the combination is off-label.
Vyvanse label: serotonin syndrome reported with SSRIs; amphetamine is also a CYP2D6 substrate.
Additive hypotension and sedation.
Stimulant against a sedating antipsychotic.

L35.theme: Two triptans; propranolol on rizatriptan; TCA + triptan; three-component barbiturate product; overuse

expected.why: Do not use two triptans within 24 hours; additive vasoconstriction, coronary spasm.
Propranolol raises rizatriptan plasma concentration about 70%; Maxalt label: use the 5 mg dose, max 15 mg/day.
Triptan + tricyclic; FDA 2006 alert.
Barbiturate + tricyclic + topiramate: sedation, cognitive slowing.
Three components. Acetaminophen 1,950 mg/day max is under the ceiling; butalbital 300 mg/day used daily -> dependence and medication-overuse headache.

L36.theme: Opioid antagonist against a partial agonist; buprenorphine + benzodiazepine; a drug that should not flag

expected.why: Naltrexone blocks buprenorphine and precipitates withdrawal; Suboxone label names naltrexone. One of these prescriptions is an error.
Boxed warning. FDA also says MAT should not be withheld over it: flag and manage, do not stop buprenorphine.
Gabapentinoid + opioid; gabapentin misuse is common alongside buprenorphine.
Additive sedation.

should_not_flag: acamprosate (renally cleared; no pharmacokinetic or pharmacodynamic interaction here)

L37.theme: P-gp inhibitors on dabigatran; dronedarone on digoxin, verapamil, simvastatin; rate-control stacking

expected.why: Dronedarone raises dabigatran exposure about 1.7-2x -> bleeding. Pradaxa label: reduce to 75 mg twice daily when CrCl is 30-50 mL/min; avoid below that.
Verapamil raises dabigatran 50-180% depending on timing; take dabigatran at least 2 hours before verapamil.
Dronedarone raises digoxin about 2.5x; Multaq label: halve digoxin and monitor levels.
Verapamil raises digoxin 50-75%.
Verapamil (CYP3A4 inhibitor) raises dronedarone about 1.4x; additive AV block. Multaq label: start non-DHP calcium channel blockers low.
Multaq label: simvastatin max 10 mg.
Zocor label: max 10 mg with verapamil.
Hypokalemia potentiates digoxin toxicity and dronedarone QT/torsades.

L38.theme: Hidden duplicate: active metabolite prescribed alongside its parent; three antipsychotics

expected.why: Paliperidone is 9-hydroxyrisperidone, risperidone's active metabolite. Prescribing both is one drug twice: 4 mg risperidone plus 6 mg paliperidone.
Three antipsychotics: additive EPS, QT, hyperprolactinemia, metabolic effects, NMS risk, no evidence of benefit.
Additive anticholinergic effects; benztropine can also mask tardive dyskinesia.
Additive sedation (the major warning is for IM olanzapine with a parenteral benzodiazepine).

L39.theme: Macrolide on colchicine and simvastatin; diltiazem as a second CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitor; QT

expected.why: Erythromycin (CYP3A4 + P-gp inhibitor) raises colchicine to toxic levels; fatal cases reported. Colcrys label: cut the dose (prophylaxis 0.3 mg/day) and never combine with renal or hepatic impairment.
Zocor label contraindicates erythromycin.
Zocor label: max 10 mg simvastatin with diltiazem; 40 mg here.
Moderate CYP3A4/P-gp inhibitor; Colcrys label: dose reduction.
Additive myotoxicity, worse with both boosted by erythromycin.
Diltiazem blocks erythromycin clearance; erythromycin + a CYP3A4 inhibitor carried about 5x the sudden cardiac death rate (Ray et al., NEJM 2004).
Hypokalemia amplifies QT risk.

L40.theme: Three bedtime hypnotics plus a benzodiazepine; SSRI at its maximum with trazodone

expected.why: Three sedative-hypnotics at bedtime plus a benzodiazepine: next-day impairment, complex sleep behaviors (zolpidem boxed warning), respiratory depression. Belsomra label: reduce dose with other CNS depressants.
Both serotonergic; sertraline at its 200 mg labeled maximum.
Dose-related; 100 mg alone is low risk. Flag only if the app tracks QT burden.
200 mg is the labeled maximum, not over it; a ceiling check should pass.

L41.theme: Data-entry traps: brand and generic of one drug; same dose in different units; one ingredient under two brands

expected.why: Same drug entered twice, once as Zoloft and once as generic. Either a data-entry duplicate or a real 100 mg/day. The app should ask, not silently sum or silently drop.
0.1 mg = 100 mcg. Same drug, same dose, twice. Units must be normalized before deduplication.
One molecule under two brands: 2,400 + 800 = 3,200 mg/day, exactly the prescription ceiling.
SSRI + NSAID GI bleeding.

totals.sertraline: 100 mg if both lines are real
totals.levothyroxine: 200 mcg if both lines are real (0.1 mg + 100 mcg)

should_not_flag: levothyroxine with sertraline at moderate or above
